canonicalExplanation.summary: Some properties **inherit**: if an element has no value of its own, it takes its parent's computed value. Text-related ones mostly do (`color`, `font-family`, `line-height`); box-related ones mostly don't (`margin`, `padding`, `border`, `width`), falling back to their **initial** value instead. You can force either with `inherit` or `initial`, and `unset` picks whichever is natural. Relative values like `em` are turned into absolute **computed** values before they're passed down.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You set `article { color: #333; margin: 2rem; }`. Every paragraph inside turns dark grey — but none of them get a 2rem margin. Why does one property travel down the tree and the other doesn't? Setting color on an article reaches ordinary descendant text, but margin does not automatically propagate. In this lesson you'll trace a property's specified and computed value through an element tree.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Elements, attributes and nesting**, **Specificity and source order**, and **Document tree and DOM concept** — inheritance follows the DOM tree from parent to child.

sections.heading: The model: missing value → parent's computed value (if inherited)
sections.body:
```css article { color: #333; font-size: 20px; margin: 2rem; } article p { font-size: 0.8em; } ``` | Property on `

` | Specified | Computed | |---|---|---| | color. | none → inherits. | #333. | | font-size. | 0.8em. | 16px (0.8 × 20px). | | margin. | none → not inherited. | initial (0) plus browser default for p. | The child inherits **16px**, not "0.8em" — grandchildren get the resolved number. ```reveal {"prompt": "How do you make a link use its parent's colour instead of the browser's blue?", "answer": "`a { color: inherit; }` — the keyword forces inheritance for that property."} ```

sections.heading: The keywords

includes: Predict which properties inherit and trace computed values down the tree.
Use inherit, initial and unset deliberately.
excludes: The revert and revert-layer keywords in depth.

outcomes: Trace a property's specified and computed value through an element tree.

examples.title: Color flows down, margin doesn't
examples.situation: Setting color on an article reaches ordinary descendant text, but margin does not automatically propagate.
walkthrough: **Color:** `article { color: #333 }`; each p has no color of its own, so it inherits #333.
**Margin:** `margin: 2rem` applies to the article's box only; margin does not inherit, so each p keeps its own default margin.
**Check:** DevTools Computed pane will show color #333 "inherited from article" and no inherited margin.
examples.result: All descendant text is dark grey, while only the article itself has the 2rem margin.

examples.title: The shrinking nested list
examples.situation: `li { font-size: 0.9em; }` with lists nested three deep — the innermost text becomes tiny.
walkthrough: Each li's 0.9em is computed from its parent's already-computed size.
Fix: use `0.9rem` (relative to the root, not the parent) so every level computes to 14.4px.
examples.result: Nested list items all compute to the same readable size.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every CSS property applied to a parent automatically applies to all descendants.
misconceptions.correction: Only inherited properties (mostly text-related, like color and font) pass down; box properties like margin, padding, border and width don't, and use their initial value unless set. Children inherit the parent's computed value.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Color flows down, margin doesn't", which property reached the paragraphs?

analogy.example: Inheritance is like **family traits**: children inherit eye colour (color, font) from parents automatically, but not their house or car (margin, border). And they inherit the actual colour, not the instructions for mixing it (computed values).
usefulFor: remembering text traits pass down, box traits don't
computed values are passed, not formulas
limitations: Families can't choose traits; CSS can force them with inherit.

steps.explanation: Setting color on an article reaches ordinary descendant text.
The relative value is computed from the parent's 20px before being passed on.
Margin does not automatically propagate to descendants.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing specified and computed values. Step 1, Color: p specified is none; p computed is #333 (inherited). Setting color on an article reaches ordinary descendant text. Step 2, Font size: specified is 0.8em; computed is 16px. The relative value is computed from the parent's 20px before being passed on. Step 3, Margin: p margin is not inherited from article. Margin does not automatically propagate to descendants.

nearTransfer.prompt: `body { font-family: Georgia; line-height: 1.5; padding: 1rem; }`. Which of these do headings, links and inputs inside the body get?
expectedEvidence: Headings and links inherit font-family and line-height; nobody inherits padding.
Inputs don't inherit font-family unless you set font: inherit.

remediation.explanation: For a property on a child, ask: **Is it set on the child? If not, does this property inherit? If yes → parent's computed value; if no → initial value.**
remediation.retryPrompt: Walk this for "The shrinking nested list".

recap.summary: To trace a property's specified and computed value through an element tree, check whether the element sets it; if not, inherited properties take the parent's computed value and non-inherited ones use their initial value. Use inherit, initial and unset to override the default behaviour.
retrievalPrompts: What does a child inherit: 0.8em or the computed pixels?
